newsitem.title: GERMANY: Minister cannot rule out Bonn may quit Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: Minister cannot rule out Bonn may quit Eurofighter.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe declined to rule out in a newspaper interview on Monday that Germany could pull out of the multinational Eurofighter project because of problems reining in its budget deficit.

Ruehe wants Bonn to buy 180 Eurofighters for 23 billion marks ($13.5 billion) from a multinational consortium including Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace (DASA), a unit of industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG.

But Finance Minister Theo Waigel is almost certain to call for more budget cuts next month after news that tax revenues are likely to fall 50 billion marks short of budget in 1997 and 1998, making it even harder to qualify for Europe's single currency.
Asked if Germany was now set to pull out of the project, Ruehe told the daily Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung: "I don't want to speculate on that now. But no one can rule it out.

"A project that will run for 20 years and cost about 20 billion marks needs a solid basis. For me, that is a cast-iron condition...I can't mothball the army or sink ships in the navy on account of the aircraft," he said, in an interview released ahead of publication in Tuesday's edition.
Ruehe said the decision had to be taken in the next few weeks, together with the passage of the 1998 budget.
Above all, he said, there was no room for further savings in the already stretched defence budget.
This meant that there could be no further cut in the medium-term budgets for other sections of the German armed forces,he said.
DASA's partners in the Eurofighter consortium are British Aerospace, Alenia Spa of Italy and state-owned CASA of Spain.
